outcome.technical: tools/reach-diff.py. (1) `--head WORKTREE`, that exact spelling: export_worktree() copies what `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` lists. Tracked files are copied as they are on disk, untracked files git does not ignore are copied, tracked files deleted on disk are skipped, symlinks are copied as links, and gitlink directories are not copied, as git archive does not copy them. The checkout and its index are never written: in the real WORKTREE run below, `git status --porcelain` was byte-identical before and after (cmp). `--base WORKTREE` refuses with 2, checked inside compare() so a direct call refuses too. The revision line shows 'the working tree over <HEAD sha>'. (2) The killed-child rule. The hook records the block label (REACH_DIFF_BLOCK, set per job), and untraced_children() now counts per block. blind_spots() rule: an untraced module child is a refusal (exit 2) unless its block ran at both revisions with the same untraced count; such a matched block is printed as a blind spot and the comparison goes on. I picked this over `--allow-untraced`: it needs no input, and a block deleted at head, whose children were untraced at base, cannot pass. Its counts differ by construction (base n, head 0), so it is unmatched and refuses. An allow flag naming that block would pass it. The rule is stated in the docstring's untraced paragraph. Docstring: a new 'THE HEAD A GATE NAMES IS THE WORKING TREE' section, usage `--head <rev|WORKTREE>`, the measuring sentence and the refusal summary updated. CONTRIBUTING.md bullet: the example now uses `--head WORKTREE`, says a gate on a task's change names `--head WORKTREE` and why (`--head HEAD` measures the last commit), says the head is copied as git lists it, and names the matched blind spot. I did NOT edit the plan or other tasks' gates: the brief's description asks for that re-pointing, the coordinator's message says not to, and those files are outside this task's scope.
